title: Asking for directions
goal: Ask for and give directions using the imperative, and get around on public transportation.
bekal: forming commands from three verb forms
giving directions: turn, straight on, as far as
asking questions and understanding the answers on the street
wave: Review **Unit 15** first: name five things you like and five you don't, each at a different strength of liking.

dialogs.title: Dialogue — Perdu dans le centre-ville
dialogs.intro: Budi is lost looking for a museum. He asks a man on the sidewalk.

lines.speaker: Budi:
lines.text: Pardon, monsieur. Je cherche le musée des Beaux-Arts.
lines.id: Excuse me, sir. I'm looking for the Museum of Fine Arts.
lines.literal: pardon, sir. I search the museum of-the beautiful-arts.

lines.speaker: Passant:
lines.text: Ah, ce n'est pas loin. Continuez tout droit.
lines.id: Oh, it's not far. Keep going straight.
lines.literal: ah, it not-is not far. continue all straight.

lines.speaker: Budi:
lines.id: Straight on as far as where?

lines.speaker: Passant:
lines.text: Jusqu'au feu rouge. Puis tournez à gauche.
lines.id: To the red light. Then turn left.
lines.literal: until-to-the light red. then turn at left.

lines.speaker: Passant:
lines.text: Prenez la deuxième rue à droite, après la pharmacie.
lines.id: Take the second street on the right, after the pharmacy.
lines.literal: take the second street at right, after the pharmacy.

lines.speaker: Budi:
lines.text: Et le musée est dans cette rue ?
lines.id: And the museum is on that street?
lines.literal: and the museum is in this street?

lines.speaker: Passant:
lines.text: Oui, au bout, sur la place. Vous ne pouvez pas le rater.
lines.id: Yes, at the end, on the square. You can't miss it.
lines.literal: yes, at-the end, on the square. you not can not it miss.

lines.speaker: Passant:
lines.text: Dix minutes, pas plus. Sinon, prenez le tram, ligne deux.
lines.id: Ten minutes, no more. Otherwise, take the tram, line two.
lines.literal: ten minutes, not more. if-not, take the tram, line two.

lines.speaker: Budi:
lines.text: Merci beaucoup, monsieur. Vous êtes très gentil.
lines.id: Thank you so much, sir. That's very kind of you.
lines.literal: thanks many, sir. you are very kind.

lines.speaker: Passant:
lines.text: Je vous en prie. Bonne visite !
lines.literal: I you of-it beg. good visit!

notes: **Commands are made by dropping the pronoun.** *Tu tournes* → *Tourne !*; *vous tournez* → *Tournez !*; *nous tournons* → *Tournons !* No new forms to memorize — just delete *tu*, *vous*, or *nous*, the way English "you turn" becomes "Turn!".
**⚠️ -er verbs drop the s in the tu form.** *Tu parles* → *Parle !*, *tu vas* → *Va !*. Only the -er group (and *aller*) does this; the others keep their s: *tu finis* → *Finis !*
**With strangers, always use the vous form.** *Tournez*, *prenez*, *continuez*. Using *tu* with someone you just met on the street sounds rude — and the imperative makes it feel twice as blunt.

**Pardon is how you start a conversation on the street.** Its cousin is *excusez-moi*. Always follow it with *monsieur* or *madame* — the French feel properly addressed, and the answer usually becomes longer and more helpful.
**Jusqu'au feu rouge** — *jusqu'à* merges with the article just like *à*: *jusqu'**au** feu*, *jusqu'**à la** gare*, *jusqu'**aux** feux*.
**La deuxième rue** — ordinal numbers are made by adding **-ième**: *deux → deuxième*, *trois → troisième*. The only exception is the first: *premier / première*.
**Vous ne pouvez pas le rater** = "you can't miss it". The standard line of direction-givers all over France — and, sadly, not always true.

grammars.title: The imperative
body: Just three forms, all taken from the present tense you already know.
after: The negative wraps around as usual: *Ne tourne pas !*, *N'ayez pas peur !*

*Être* and *avoir* have their own imperatives that must be memorized — but both are rare outside set phrases: *Sois sage !* (be good), *N'aie pas peur !* (don't be afraid), *Soyez le bienvenu !* (welcome).
Reflexive verbs put the pronoun **after** the verb with a hyphen: *Lève-**toi** !*, *Asseyez-**vous** !*, *Dépêche-**toi** !* But in the negative, it moves back in front: *Ne te lève pas !*

grammars.title: Direction words
body: What French people actually say when giving directions.
after: ⚠️ *À droite* (to the right) and *tout droit* (straight on) differ by just one word and are easily confused. Mishearing at an intersection can send you to the wrong end of town.
Ordinal numbers: *premier/première, deuxième, troisième, quatrième, cinquième*. From *cinq* up, just add -ième, with small spelling adjustments (*neuf → neuvième*).

blocks.title: Lifesaving phrases
items: *Pardon, où est la gare, s'il vous plaît ?* — Excuse me, where is the station?
*Je cherche cette adresse.* — I'm looking for this address.
*C'est loin d'ici ?* — Is it far from here?
*Quel bus va au centre-ville ?* — Which bus goes downtown?
*Vous pouvez répéter plus lentement, s'il vous plaît ?* — Could you repeat that more slowly?
*Un aller-retour pour Paris, s'il vous plaît.* — A round-trip ticket to Paris, please.

blocks.text: The last phrase in that box — *plus lentement* — may be the most useful in the whole unit. French people speak fast, and asking them to slow down is perfectly normal.

vocab.en: to the right / to the left

exercises.prompt: Fill in the blanks with the right direction word.
items: Le musée est ____ bout de la rue.
Excuse me, where is the station?
Keep going straight to the red light.
Could you repeat that more slowly?

Parle plus lentement. — Finis ton travail. — Va à la gare. — Attends ici. — Lève-toi.
